name: M1 Garand Rifle Squad
note: The M1 Garand was the first semi-automatic rifle issued as standard to any army, giving American rifle squads a high rate of fire.

name: M4 Sherman
note: The main American medium tank. About 50,000 were built, and it served with most Allied armies.

name: M1 57mm Gun Team
note: An American-built version of the British 6-pounder anti-tank gun.

name: M2A1 105mm Howitzer Battery
note: The standard American divisional howitzer, valued for its accuracy and rate of fire.

name: P-47 Thunderbolt Flight
note: A heavy, rugged fighter used widely for ground attack as well as bomber escort.

name: M8 Greyhound
note: A six-wheeled armored car with a 37 mm gun, used by cavalry reconnaissance troops.

name: WC-54 Ambulance Team
note: The Dodge WC-54 was the US Army's main field ambulance.

name: Combat Engineer Platoon
note: Engineers built bridges and roads, cleared mines and breached obstacles close behind the fighting.

name: GMC CCKW Truck Section
note: The 2½-ton "deuce and a half" truck carried most American supplies overland.

name: Lee-Enfield Rifle Section
note: The bolt-action Lee-Enfield could be fired quickly by a trained rifleman and served throughout the war.

name: Cromwell
note: A fast cruiser tank powered by the Rolls-Royce Meteor engine, in action from 1944.

name: 6-pounder Gun Team
note: A 57 mm anti-tank gun that replaced the 2-pounder from 1942.

name: 25-pounder Battery
note: The standard British field gun-howitzer, known for its versatility.

name: Hawker Typhoon Flight
note: The Typhoon became the RAF's principal ground-attack aircraft, armed with cannon and rockets.

name: Bren Carrier Scout Section
note: The Universal Carrier, a small tracked vehicle built in greater numbers than any other armored vehicle.

name: Austin K2 Ambulance Team
note: The Austin K2/Y was the standard British heavy ambulance, nicknamed "Katy".

name: Royal Engineers Section
note: The Royal Engineers, known as "sappers", built, bridged and cleared the way for the army.

name: Bedford QL Lorry Section
note: A four-wheel-drive 3-ton lorry and a workhorse of British transport.

name: Guards Rifle Squad
note: "Guards" was an honorary title given to Soviet units that distinguished themselves in battle.

name: T-34
note: A medium tank that combined sloped armor, a powerful gun and wide tracks, built in very large numbers.

name: ZiS-2 57mm Gun Team
note: A powerful 57 mm anti-tank gun.

name: BM-13 Katyusha Battery
note: A truck-mounted multiple rocket launcher, nicknamed "Katyusha".

name: Il-2 Shturmovik Flight
note: A heavily armored ground-attack aircraft, built in greater numbers than any other combat aircraft of the war.

name: BA-64 Armored Car
note: A small four-wheel-drive armored car.

name: GAZ-55 Ambulance Team
note: An ambulance built on the GAZ-AA truck chassis.

name: Sapper Platoon
note: Soviet sappers cleared mines, built crossings and prepared defences.

name: GAZ-AA Truck Column
note: A 1.5-ton truck based on a Ford design, known as the "polutorka".

name: Panzergrenadier Squad
note: Panzergrenadiers were the motorised and mechanised infantry who fought alongside the tanks.

name: Panzer IV
note: The only German tank to remain in production throughout the war.

name: Pak 40 Team
note: The standard German 75 mm anti-tank gun from 1942.

name: leFH 18 Howitzer Battery
note: The standard German 105 mm light field howitzer.

name: Fw 190 Flight
note: A radial-engined fighter that was also widely used as a fighter-bomber.

name: Sd.Kfz. 222 Armored Car
note: A light four-wheeled armored car with a 20 mm cannon.

name: Field Ambulance Team
note: Medical teams collected the wounded close to the fighting and moved them back to field hospitals.

name: Pionier Platoon
note: German combat engineers, trained for assault as well as construction.

name: Opel Blitz Truck Column
note: The standard German 3-ton truck.

name: Chasseurs Squad
note: Chasseurs were the light infantry of the French Army.

name: Char B1 bis
note: A heavy tank with a 75 mm gun in the hull and a 47 mm gun in the turret.

name: 47mm SA 37 Gun Team
note: An effective French 47 mm anti-tank gun of 1940.

name: Canon de 75 Battery
note: The famous quick-firing 75 mm field gun of 1897, still in service in 1940.

name: Dewoitine D.520 Flight
note: The best French fighter available in 1940.

name: Panhard 178
note: A fast four-wheeled armored car.

name: Service de Santé Team
note: The Service de Santé was the French Army's medical service.

name: Génie Platoon
note: The Génie was the French Army's engineer arm.

name: Citroën U23 Truck Section
note: A light truck widely used by the French Army.

name: Bersaglieri Squad
note: Light infantry known for their wide-brimmed hats with black feathers and for moving at the run.

name: M13/40
note: The main Italian medium tank of the North African campaign.

name: 47/32 Gun Team
note: A light 47 mm gun used both against tanks and to support infantry.

name: Semovente 75/18
note: A self-propelled gun that proved effective in both artillery and anti-tank roles.

name: Macchi C.202 Flight
note: The "Folgore", an agile fighter with a licence-built German engine.

name: AB 41 Armored Car
note: A four-wheel-drive armored car with a 20 mm cannon and a driving position at each end.

name: Sanità Ambulance Team
note: Medical teams collected the wounded close to the fighting and moved them back to field hospitals.

name: Genio Pioneer Platoon
note: The Genio was the engineer arm of the Italian Army.

name: Fiat 626 Truck Section
note: A medium truck used throughout the Italian Army.

name: Rifle Section
note: Japanese rifle sections were armed with Arisaka bolt-action rifles.

name: Type 97 Chi-Ha
note: The most widely produced Japanese medium tank.

name: Type 1 47mm Gun Team
note: Japan's main purpose-built anti-tank gun.

name: Type 92 Battalion Gun
note: A small 70 mm infantry gun, light enough to be manhandled.

name: Ki-43 Hayabusa Flight
note: The Army's "Hayabusa" fighter, noted for its manoeuvrability.

name: Type 97 Te-Ke Tankette
note: A small two-man tankette.

name: Field Medical Team
note: Medical teams collected the wounded close to the fighting and moved them back to field hospitals.

name: Engineer Platoon
note: Engineers built bridges and roads, cleared mines and breached obstacles close behind the fighting.

name: Type 94 Truck Section
note: A six-wheeled army truck.

name: Fletcher-class Destroyer
note: A large and successful class of American destroyers; 175 were completed.

name: Flower-class Corvette
note: Small escort ships based on a whale-catcher design, built to protect convoys.

name: G-5 Torpedo Boat Flight
note: A small, very fast torpedo boat.

name: S-boat Flotilla
note: Fast torpedo boats, which the Allies called E-boats.

name: Le Fantasque-class Destroyer
note: Large, very fast destroyers.

name: MAS Torpedo Boat Flight
note: Small, fast motor torpedo boats.

name: Fubuki-class Destroyer
note: Destroyers that set a new standard for firepower when they were introduced.

name: Military Police Jeep Patrol
note: American military police directed traffic, guarded prisoners and kept order behind the lines.

name: Engineer Fire Fighting Platoon
note: The Corps of Engineers raised fire fighting platoons to protect depots, airfields and ports.

name: Dodge WC Command Car Section
note: Dodge WC-series command cars carried officers and their radios close to the front.

name: M26 Pershing
note: A heavy tank with a 90 mm gun that reached Europe only in the last months of the war.

name: M10 Tank Destroyer
note: A tank destroyer on the Sherman chassis, with a 3-inch gun in an open-topped turret.

name: Royal Military Police Section
note: The Royal Military Police were known as "Redcaps" for their scarlet cap covers.

name: Army Fire Service Section
note: Military fire services protected depots, airfields and installations, where fuel and ammunition made any fire dangerous.

name: AEC Dorchester Command Vehicle
note: An armoured command vehicle built on the AEC Matador chassis.

name: Churchill Mk VII
note: A slow but heavily armored infantry tank, noted for crossing difficult ground.

name: Achilles 17-pounder
note: The American M10 re-armed with the powerful British 17-pounder gun.

name: Commandant's Service Patrol
note: The commandant's service regulated military traffic and kept order in rear areas.

name: Fire Protection Detachment
note: Military fire services protected depots, airfields and installations, where fuel and ammunition made any fire dangerous.

name: GAZ-61 Staff Car Section
note: A four-wheel-drive staff car used by senior commanders.

name: IS-2
note: A heavy tank armed with a 122 mm gun, in service from 1944.

name: SU-85
note: A tank destroyer mounting an 85 mm gun on the T-34 chassis.

name: Feldgendarmerie Troop
note: Military police recognisable by the metal gorget worn on a chain around the neck.

name: Feuerschutz Detachment
note: Military fire services protected depots, airfields and installations, where fuel and ammunition made any fire dangerous.

name: Sd.Kfz. 251/6 Command Vehicle
note: A command version of the standard German half-track.

name: Tiger I
note: A heavy tank with an 88 mm gun and thick armor, first used in 1942.

name: StuG III
note: A turretless assault gun, and the most-produced German armored fighting vehicle of the war.

name: Prévôté Gendarmerie Section
note: Gendarmes attached to the army in the field served as its military police.

name: Sapeurs-Pompiers Section
note: The Paris fire brigade is a unit of the French Army.

name: Laffly V15R Command Car
note: A four-wheel-drive reconnaissance and liaison car.

name: SOMUA S35
note: A cavalry tank with cast armor, often counted among the best tanks of 1940.

name: Laffly W15 TCC
note: A 47 mm anti-tank gun mounted on a Laffly truck, improvised in 1940.

name: Carabinieri Reali Section
note: The Carabinieri also served as the army's military police.

name: Vigili del Fuoco Detachment
note: The Vigili del Fuoco are Italy's national fire service.

name: Fiat 508 CM Staff Car
note: A military version of the Fiat 508 Balilla car.

name: P26/40
note: The heaviest Italian tank of the war, completed only in small numbers.

name: Semovente 90/53
note: A 90 mm gun mounted on a tank chassis; only a few were built.

name: Military Police Section
note: Military police kept order and directed movement behind the lines.

name: Fire Defense Detachment
note: Military fire services protected depots, airfields and installations, where fuel and ammunition made any fire dangerous.

name: Type 95 Kurogane Staff Car
note: A small four-wheel-drive scout car.

name: Type 3 Chi-Nu
note: A medium tank with a 75 mm gun, kept in Japan for home defence.

name: Type 1 Ho-Ni I
note: A 75 mm gun mounted on the Chi-Ha tank chassis.

name: M5 Stuart
note: A fast light tank used mainly for reconnaissance and screening.

name: M4A3E8 Sherman
note: The "Easy Eight": a late Sherman with a 76 mm gun and improved suspension.

name: M1919 Machine-Gun Team
note: The Browning M1919 was the standard American medium machine gun.

name: M7 Priest Battery
note: A 105 mm howitzer on a tank chassis. Its pulpit-like machine-gun mount earned it the British name "Priest".

name: B-25 Mitchell Flight
note: A twin-engined medium bomber that served in every theatre.

name: Willys Jeep Recon Team
note: The quarter-ton four-wheel-drive "jeep" served as scout car, runabout and light carrier.

name: Crusader Mk III
note: A fast cruiser tank best known from North Africa; the Mk III carried a 6-pounder gun.

name: Sherman Firefly
note: A Sherman fitted with the 17-pounder gun, able to take on the heaviest German tanks.

name: Vickers Machine-Gun Section
note: A water-cooled machine gun famed for its reliability in sustained fire.

name: 5.5-inch Medium Battery
note: A medium gun that entered service in 1941 and equipped medium regiments.

name: Mosquito Flight
note: A very fast twin-engined aircraft built largely of wood.

name: Daimler Dingo Scout Car
note: A small, quiet two-man scout car.

name: T-70
note: A light tank with a two-man crew.

name: KV-1
note: A heavy tank whose thick armor made it very hard to knock out in 1941.

name: Maxim Machine-Gun Team
note: The water-cooled Maxim M1910 machine gun on its wheeled mount.

name: ML-20 152mm Battery
note: A 152 mm gun-howitzer.

name: Pe-2 Flight
note: A fast twin-engined dive bomber.

name: M-72 Motorcycle Scouts
note: A heavy motorcycle with a sidecar.

name: Panzer II
note: A light tank that made up much of the early-war panzer force.

name: Panther
note: A medium tank with sloped armor and a long 75 mm gun, introduced in 1943.

name: MG 42 Team
note: A machine gun with a very high rate of fire.

name: Nebelwerfer 41 Battery
note: A six-barrelled rocket launcher.

name: Ju 88 Flight
note: A versatile twin-engined aircraft used as a bomber, night fighter and in many other roles.

name: BMW R75 Motorcycle Scouts
note: A heavy motorcycle whose sidecar wheel was also driven.

name: Renault R35
note: A light infantry-support tank, and the most numerous French tank in 1940.

name: Hotchkiss H39
note: A light tank used by both cavalry and infantry units.

name: Hotchkiss Machine-Gun Section
note: The air-cooled Hotchkiss M1914 machine gun.

name: Canon de 155 GPF Battery
note: A long-range 155 mm gun first used in the First World War.

name: LeO 451 Flight
note: A modern, fast medium bomber of 1940.

name: Motorcycle Dragoons
note: Motorcycle troops scouted ahead of French mechanised formations.

name: L6/40
note: A light tank used for reconnaissance.

name: M15/42
note: An improved medium tank with a petrol engine and a longer gun.

name: Breda M37 Machine-Gun Team
note: A heavy machine gun fed from metal strips.

name: Cannone da 149/40 Battery
note: A modern long-range heavy gun.

name: SM.79 Sparviero Flight
note: A three-engined bomber that was especially successful as a torpedo bomber.

name: Moto Guzzi Alce Scouts
note: A sturdy military motorcycle.

name: Type 95 Ha-Go
note: A light tank used widely in China and the Pacific.

name: Type 1 Chi-He
note: An improved medium tank with a 47 mm gun.

name: Type 92 Machine-Gun Team
note: A heavy machine gun fed from metal strips.

name: Type 96 150mm Howitzer Battery
note: The Army's main heavy howitzer.

name: Ki-21 Flight
note: A twin-engined Army heavy bomber.

name: Type 97 Motorcycle Scouts
note: A military motorcycle with a sidecar.
